title: Key & Route Incident Triage Playbook (UX + Wireframe Notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook + wireframe notes for operators and product on how the Console surfaces per-key and per-route incidents, and the quick actions we want available during an active rate/quota incident. Goal is a 1-pager + wireframe that SRE/CS/Support can lean on to triage and resolve throttling/quota problems without toggling between >4 tools.

High-level objectives:
- Make root-cause discovery < 5 minutes for common cases (quota exhaustion, burst traffic, bad client loop).
- Provide safe, reversible quick actions (apply emergency throttle, temporarily bump quota, route fallback, user message).
- Preserve auditability: every operator action must be logged and attachable to a ticket.
- Surface correlated signals (errors, latency, model fallbacks) next to quota usage for faster correlation.

Target personas:
- SRE on-call: needs fast diagnostics and rollback controls.
- Support engineer: wants reproducible steps to explain to customers and temporary mitigations.
- Product/Account owner: needs visibility into an incident timeline and cost impact.

Wireframe notes (top-to-bottom):
1) Page header: single-line summary + badges
   - Title: "Incident: credential_abc123 / route: /v1/completions"
   - Badges: status (active/resolved), severity (P0/P1), affected customers (count), ETA for resolution (manual).
   - Quick-actions to right: "Acknowledge", "Create Jira", "Request quota bump" (opens modal).

2) Left column (diagnostics):
   - Compact heatmap: per-minute token usage for the key (last 6h) — hover shows tokens/min and sample requests.
   - Error & latency sparklines beneath heatmap (align time axis).
   - Top 5 routes by token contribution for this key (route name, % of tokens, p95 latency, error rate).
   - Small note: link to raw logs (observability) + sample request payload (scrubbed).

3) Middle column (root-cause helpers):
   - Automated hints (derived by heuristics): e.g., "sudden 20x traffic spike from single IP", "multiple long-sequence completions > 10k tokens", "retry loop pattern detected (same request repeated)".
   - Suggested actions (ranked): 1) Apply temporary route throttle 2) Enable model fallback 3) Invalidate KV cache (rare) 4) Ask dev to patch retry logic.
   - Button group: "Apply suggested action" (opens confirm modal with automatic audit note).

4) Right column (controls & history):
   - Live quota meter (how much of daily/monthly quota consumed; small slider to select safety margin).
   - Operator quick actions (primary):
       * Emergency throttle: choose % of baseline or set token cap per minute
       * Bump quota: +X tokens until timestamp (approval flow note)
       * Route fallback: send traffic to a cheaper model variant (list of compatible variants)
       * Rate-limit sandbox: preview effect on last 30 minutes of traffic (simulated)
   - Action history (chronological list) with operator name, timestamp, comment. Click to expand to linked Jira.

5) Bottom (postmortem starter + export):
   - One-click incident starter (populates a template with attached signals and recommended RCA points).
   - Export CSV / JSON of sampled requests and metrics for an attached ticket.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- A user can identify the top contributing route and apply an emergency throttle within 2 clicks from the incident header.
- Quick actions create auditable entries in the audit log and can be reverted by another operator.
- Hints/heuristics cover at least these classes: quota exhaustion, client-side retry loop, long-sequence runaway token consumption, region-wide surge.
- Simulated sandbox accurately shows % reduction in tokens for last 30 minutes (within ±5%).

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets & priorities):
- INFR-421 (P0): Emergency throttle control UI + backend action + audit log (owner: Jonah) — block until approve.
- INFR-422 (P1): Per-key heatmap with sample request peek (owner: Priya).
- INFR-423 (P1): Heuristic engine: detect retry loops / repeated payloads (owner: Luca).
- CONSOLE-210 (P2): Route fallback selector UI (populate compatible model variants list).
- CONSOLE-211 (P2): Rate-limit sandbox simulation (basic engine + lightweight preview) — integrate with mock traffic for UI.
- DOCS-88 (P3): Incident starter templates for Support and SRE.

UI micro-interactions / details to decide:
- Confirm modal language: always show "impact preview" and estimated token delta.
- Reversion: require 2FA/secondary confirmation for quota increases > 10% of committed capacity.
- Ownership: operator actions should include an optional "customer-facing note" field that can be copied to a ticket.

Open questions / decisions:
- Should emergency throttle be scoped to credential OR to route OR both? Suggest default to route-first (less risky) with a bolt-on to scope to credential.
- Approval flow for quota bumps: auto-approve if < X tokens and < 1h duration? Need legal/finance input.
- How to show multi-credential incidents (shared customers with several keys)? Proposed: top header shows aggregated view with per-key accordion.

Edge cases & notes to self:
- If a model fallback is applied, we need to show per-variant quality delta in the UI (estimate based on evals).
- For private deployments, quick actions should surface a note: "action will run in target VPC — contact infra".
- Keep sample payloads scrubbed by default; a toggle to show full with strict auditing.

Design sketches (very rough text sketch):
- Sketch A (compact incident): header + three columns (diag, root-cause, actions). Minimal. Good for SRE fast path.
- Sketch B (expanded): accordion for each affected key, timeline at top (zoomable), action drawer slides from right for more granular controls. Better for postmortem and product.

Suggested rollout plan:
1) Build the emergency throttle MVP (INFR-421) + basic heatmap (INFR-422) behind a feature flag.
2) Pilot with 2 SREs for 2 weeks on non-prod incidents. Collect time-to-triage metrics.
3) Iterate heuristics (INFR-423) and add sandbox simulation (CONSOLE-211).

Metrics we'll track after launch:
- Median time-to-action when incident detected (target < 5 min).
- Rate of successful mitigations (incident resolved within 30 min post-action).
- False positive rate for heuristics (ops manual override).
- Audit completeness (percent of actions with a customer-facing note).

Notes / references:
- See incident on 2025-01-08 in slack:#ops-incident-2025-01-08 — recurring retry pattern from mobile app.
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/987 (backend hooks for throttle).
- Jira items (linked above) for grooming session on 2025-01-15.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Capture legal/finance decision on auto-approving small quota bumps (owner: Marisol).
- [ ] Finalize wording on confirm modal copy (owner: UX).
- [ ] Add audit replay capability to expand past actions and their downstream effects (owner: Observability).

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep language in UI simple; operators are juggling pager + slack + console. Minimal friction is key.
- We should prioritize reversible actions first — increases are riskier than reducing traffic.

Last thoughts:
This doc is intentionally terse. Want to use the next session with SRE to iterate on the three-column layout and confirm the set of actions that can be safely automated vs requiring an approval step. Add example incident flows for common customers so Support can rehearse the playbook.
